people/john-wimber/summary: Former rock musician who became leader of the Association of Vineyard Churches. His 'power evangelism' and 'doin' the stuff' approach taught ordinary believers to pray for healing; his Fuller Seminary course with Peter Wagner popularised the Third Wave. Vineyard worship shaped contemporary music.
people/pope-francis/summary: Jorge Mario Bergoglio, Jesuit archbishop of Buenos Aires, elected in 2013 as the first pope from the Americas. His pontificate stressed mercy, care for the poor and migrants, creation (Laudato si') and synodality, provoking both enthusiasm and traditionalist opposition. He died on Easter Monday, 21 April 2025.
people/yong-gi-cho/summary: Korean Pentecostal pastor who, after healing from tuberculosis, founded Yoido Full Gospel Church in 1958, growing it through home cell groups into the world's largest congregation. He taught a 'threefold blessing' of salvation, health and prosperity; in 2014 he was convicted of embezzlement involving church funds.
people/edward-fudge/summary: American Church of Christ theologian and lawyer whose The Fire That Consumes (1982) made the evangelical case for conditional immortality — that the unsaved are finally destroyed rather than tormented eternally. It persuaded many evangelicals and provoked extended debate.
people/kwame-bediako/summary: Ghanaian Presbyterian theologian who founded the Akrofi-Christaller Institute at Akropong. In Theology and Identity and Christianity in Africa he argued that African Christianity is a 'non-Western religion' continuous with pre-Christian African religious heritage, like the early church's engagement with Hellenism.
people/john-piper/summary: Long-time pastor of Bethlehem Baptist Church in Minneapolis and founder of Desiring God, whose Desiring God (1986) propounded 'Christian hedonism'. A leading voice of the 'young, restless, Reformed' movement, he defends Calvinist soteriology, penal substitution and complementarianism.
people/n-t-wright/summary: English New Testament scholar and former bishop of Durham, a leading figure in the 'New Perspective on Paul'. His Christian Origins and the Question of God series argues for the historical Jesus as Israel's Messiah and for bodily resurrection, and he reframes justification around covenant membership.
people/n-t-wright/keyIdeas/2: Jesus and the story of Israel
people/c-baxter-kruger/summary: American theologian and director of Perichoresis, whose books such as The Great Dance and The Shack Revisited popularise a 'Trinitarian theology' emphasising humanity's adoption into the life of the Trinity through Christ, drawing on Athanasius and the Torrances. Critics see in it a tendency toward universalism.
people/francois-du-toit/summary: South African teacher of the 'Mirror Word' movement and author of The Mirror Bible, a paraphrase of the New Testament emphasising humanity's union with Christ through his death and resurrection. His teaching is often associated with 'finished work' and universalist-leaning views that many evangelicals reject.
people/francois-du-toit/keyIdeas/0: Union with Christ of all humanity
people/francois-du-toit/keyIdeas/1: Mirror reflection of identity in Christ
people/rob-bell/summary: Founding pastor of Mars Hill Bible Church in Michigan, whose Love Wins (2011) questioned traditional teaching on eternal punishment and suggested God's love may ultimately reconcile all. The book provoked fierce controversy among evangelicals; he left the church in 2012.
